correctness.rationale: For each fixed angular Fourier shift k, polar integration gives exact monomial Toeplitz matrix coefficient as a normalized Beta integral. Substituting u=n(1-r²) makes the nonnegative weights converge in L1 to a Gamma(alpha+1,1) density even when -1<alpha<0. After removing the deterministic phase beta[1+log n]^gamma by diagonal gauge, the phase relative to log u tends to zero at gamma<1, to u^(ik beta) at gamma=1, and becomes nonstationary with derivative order (log n)^(gamma-1)/u for gamma>1. Hence Fourier coefficients tend to 1, Gamma(alpha+1+ik beta)/Gamma(alpha+1), or zero (k≠0). Each trigonometric polynomial yields finite weighted shifts with convergent weights and compact difference; norm density extends to continuous f. Continuous Hardy Toeplitz extension then supplies the stated Fredholm essential spectrum/norm and index. Gamma has no zeros, giving the sharp compactness iff gamma>1 for nonconstant f after subtracting f0. Independently numerically integrated original Beta coefficient and dephased values for n=25,100,400, gamma=.65,1,1.6 with alpha=0 beta=1.3; critical values approach |Gamma(1+1.3i)| and supercritical magnitude decays .0120,.00297,.00084. The finite tests corroborate, not prove, the infinite normal form.

Quiroga-Barranco supplies general monomial matrix integral formulas for quasi-homogeneous weighted Bergman Toeplitz operators, not the explicit logarithmically winding disk-symbol triple threshold or log-Gamma multiplier. Hagger gives an abstract limit-operator Fredholm criterion; computing exact symbol limits and the diagonal gauge for this spiral family is new relative to its stated results. Esmeral-Maximenko-Vasilevski treat angular Toeplitz operators on the upper half-plane, and Taskinen periodic planar domains; neither is the same nonlinear angular-spiral disk family. Resultary search found related radial Mellin spectral examples but not a covering angular Fredholm theorem. Strong generic limit-operator methods and any historical spiral-symbol classification remain priority risks.
